around.headline: AI deepfake video call impersonating Tamil Nadu CM Vijay costs Bengaluru man Rs 1 lakh
around.summary: A fraudster used an AI deepfake video call that looked and sounded like Tamil Nadu CM Vijay to promise a Bengaluru man Rs 11 lakh in government aid, getting him to transfer Rs 1 lakh first before vanishing — a CB-CID case for the same deepfake was already registered on Sept 2, per TOI and The420.in. No genuine welfare scheme ever asks the beneficiary to pay a fee before the money is released, however convincing the caller looks.

around.headline: Counterfeit cancer drugs sold at steep discount traced to 90+ Bengaluru hospitals, pharmacy owner arrested
around.summary: A large haul of counterfeit chemotherapy medicines, sold at roughly half the market price, was traced to a private facility supplying more than 90 Bengaluru hospitals, and its pharmacy owner has been arrested, per India Today, The Hindu and The Indian Express. Buy critical drugs only from hospital pharmacies or verified chains, and treat a steep discount on a cancer or chronic-care medicine as a warning sign, not a bargain.
around.source: India Today, The Hindu, The Indian Express

around.headline: Nurse and friend lose Rs 29.8 lakh to an online investment scam
around.summary: A Bengaluru nurse and her friend lost a combined Rs 29.8 lakh to an online investment scam, per Deccan Herald. Treat any app or 'advisor' promising guaranteed high returns as a red flag, and check it's SEBI-registered before transferring money.

around.headline: Ulsoor Lake readies for immersion of 1 lakh Ganesha idols as festival week peaks
around.summary: Bengaluru's rejuvenated Ulsoor Lake is set to receive roughly 1 lakh Ganesha idols for immersion as the festival wraps up, per TOI, adding to crowds and diversions already reported around flyovers and the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway tolls. Build in extra time or an alternate route if you're passing near major lakes or immersion points through the week.

around.headline: Consumer forum orders company to pay Rs 1.8 lakh over false cosmetic-treatment claims
around.summary: A Bengaluru woman won Rs 1.8 lakh after a consumer forum ruled that a company's cosmetic-treatment promises amounted to false advertising, per TOI. Keep receipts and the specific claims made in ads for any paid service — a consumer forum complaint can get your money back well after the fact.

around.headline: PM Modi and China's Xi Jinping push business ties and border peace as relations thaw
around.summary: PM Modi and China's Xi Jinping used a summit meeting to push closer business links and border peace as India-China relations continue to thaw, per Reuters. A calmer border and reopening trade channels could mean steadier supply and pricing for Chinese-made electronics and components in the months ahead.

street_smart.title: You get a WhatsApp video call from an unfamiliar number. The face and voice on screen are unmistakably a sitting Chief Minister's — he congratulates you personally on being selected for an ₹11 lakh government relief payout, and says a ₹1 lakh 'processing and verification fee' needs to go out first before the aid can be released to your account. What's the smartest thing to do?
street_smart.based_on: TOI Bengaluru and The420.in, Sept 13 — an AI deepfake video call impersonating Tamil Nadu CM Vijay promised a Bengaluru man Rs 11 lakh in government aid; he transferred Rs 1 lakh before realizing it was fraud, and a CB-CID case for the same deepfake had already been registered on Sept 2. This AI-deepfake advance-fee-scam mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks (the closest, Aug 29, was a bank-fraud phone call — a different mechanism with no video or deepfake involved).
street_smart.situation: The call quality is sharp, the CM's mannerisms and voice match what you've seen on TV, and a second person joins briefly claiming to be a 'department aide' confirming the scheme.

choices.text: Hang up without sending any money. Verify the scheme only by calling the department's official helpline or checking its listing on the state government's website, and if the call persists, report the number and a screen recording to the cyber crime helpline (1930) or cybercrime.gov.in.
choices.feedback: Correct. No genuine government welfare or relief scheme ever asks the beneficiary to pay a fee before the money is released — that single rule holds regardless of who appears to be asking, and it's the only check that a realistic deepfake can't get around.

choices.text: Since the video and voice look and sound exactly like the real CM, and the 'department aide' vouches for it on the call, you transfer the Rs 1 lakh fee so the Rs 11 lakh aid gets released.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. A hyper-realistic face and voice on a video call is no longer proof of identity — AI deepfakes can convincingly mimic a real chief minister in real time, and once you pay, the number goes dead and the aid never arrives, exactly as happened to a Bengaluru man on Sept 13.

choices.text: You ask the caller for official proof of the scheme, and once they send over a scanned 'government order' PDF that looks authentic, you go ahead and pay the fee since you now have documentation.
choices.feedback: Risky. Scammers can fabricate a convincing fake PDF just as easily as a deepfake video call — a document sent to you by the same caller is not independent verification; only checking directly with the department or its official helpline is.

choices.text: You don't pay anything, but you also don't report it — you just block the number and move on.
choices.feedback: Risky. Blocking the number protects only you; without a report to the cyber crime helpline (1930), the same deepfake script keeps working on the next person, and investigators lose a lead for the CB-CID case already open on this scam.

takeaways: Government welfare or relief schemes never require the beneficiary to pay a fee first — that 'processing charge' request is always the scam, whoever appears to be asking for it.

A realistic face or voice on a call is no longer proof of identity — AI deepfakes can mimic a real public figure in real time, so verify independently through the official department website or helpline rather than through anything the caller sends you.
Report scheme-related scam calls immediately to the national cyber crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in — fast reporting is what lets banks freeze the transferred money before it's withdrawn.

quiz.question: Which state's Chief Minister was impersonated in the AI deepfake WhatsApp video call scam that cost a Bengaluru man Rs 1 lakh this week?
quiz.why: A CB-CID case over the same deepfake impersonation had already been registered on Sept 2, before this latest victim came forward.

quiz.question: Roughly how many Bengaluru hospitals came under the scanner after counterfeit cancer drugs were traced to a facility supplying them at a steep discount?
quiz.why: Buying critical medicines only from hospital pharmacies or licensed chains is the simplest guard against counterfeit drugs.

quiz.question: Which world leader did PM Modi meet this week to push closer business ties and border peace, marking a further thaw in relations?
quiz.why: Warmer India-China ties could ease trade friction on everything from electronics components to rare-earth supplies.

quiz.question: Which body actually conducts elections to Bengaluru's civic body (BBMP/GBA), as distinct from the Election Commission of India?
quiz.why: Each state has its own State Election Commission for local-body polls — Bengaluru has gone without an elected civic council for years partly because these elections keep getting delayed.

quiz.question: Under India's Consumer Protection Act, within how many years of a purchase must you typically file a complaint with a consumer forum?
quiz.why: That's the same window a Bengaluru woman used this week to win Rs 1.8 lakh after a company's cosmetic-treatment claims turned out to be false advertising.
